q: What does CBAM mean for a US steel exporter with no federal carbon price?
title: US steel exports and EU CBAM
short: US steel entering the EU falls under CBAM, and with no national carbon price there is usually nothing to deduct. Electric arc furnace mills often have lower direct emissions than blast furnace routes, so reporting verified actual figures, rather than defaults, matters for their buyers.
audience: US steel exporters and EU importers of US steel

ul: Direct embedded emissions per tonne, plus precursors such as bought slab or DRI.
No deduction unless a carbon price was effectively paid.

p: Some state programmes cover power plants, not steel mills, so they rarely create a deductible price for steel.
Prepare a verified figure per installation and product route.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, power and production records into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions your EU importer asks for.

sources.label: European Commission, CBAM legislation and guidance
